target: Hej allihopa, jag hoppas att ni alla har det bra.
english: Hi everyone, I hope you all are doing well.
tip: Hoppas always ends in -s though its meaning is active: jag hoppas att ni har det bra.

target: Jag är glad att du kunde komma hit till oss.
english: I'm glad you could come visit us.
tip: hit = to here (movement toward the speaker); här is the static 'here': komma hit.

target: Tack för att du tog dig tid att träffa mig.
english: Thank you for taking the time to meet me.
tip: ta sig tid = make time; the reflexive dig is required: du tog dig tid.

target: Jag har haft ont i huvudet sedan tidigt i morse.
english: I have had a headache since early this morning.
tip: Pain is ha ont i: har haft ont i huvudet = have had a headache, literally have bad in the head.

english: We sing Christmas carols in December.
tip: Months take i: i december = in December, i juli = in July.

target: Han är medveten om att han måste ändra sina vanor.
english: He is aware that he needs to change his habits.
tip: medveten om = aware of; this adjective fixes its preposition as om: medveten om att han måste ändra.

target: Vi sparar pengar varje månad för att kunna resa mer.
english: We save money every month in order to travel more.
tip: Kan has the infinitive kunna, used after another verb: för att kunna resa = to be able to travel.

target: Vi har tre barn som alla går i skolan här.
english: We have three children who all go to school here.
tip: Gå i skolan (in) means be a pupil; gå till skolan (to) is the trip. Here: alla går i skolan.

target: Välkommen hit, vi har förberett ett rum åt dig här.
english: Welcome, we have prepared a room for you.
tip: åt marks who benefits: ett rum åt dig = a room for you.

target: Min syster och jag brukar ringa varandra varje söndag kväll.
english: My sister and I usually call each other every Sunday evening.
tip: 'Brukar' (usually do) – a uniquely Swedish verb meaning habitual action. No direct English equivalent.

target: Igår gick vi till den nya restaurangen nere vid hamnen.
english: Yesterday we went to the new restaurant down by the harbor.
tip: nere = down as a location; ner is down as motion: nere vid hamnen.

target: Rummet på hotellet var rent och hade en bekväm säng.
english: The room at the hotel was clean and had a comfortable bed.
tip: Adjectives add -t with ett-words: rummet var rent = the room was clean.
Swedish stacks nouns into one: havregrynsgröt is havre plus gryn plus gröt, oatmeal porridge.

target: Du skämtar väl inte med mig om det här?
english: You are surely not joking with me about this?
tip: In a main clause the verb comes before inte: du skämtar inte. In a subordinate clause (att, om, som) it flips to inte before the verb.
The verb keeps second place even when another word leads: September börjar hösten.
With åka, transport takes no article: åker spårvagn = take the tram, åker buss = take the bus.
Jobs drop the article after är: Hon är läkare, not en läkare.
The -s ending makes it passive: laddas = is being charged, from ladda = to charge.
"Varm" → "varmt" for ett-words. The -t makes it neuter.
känna sig means feel; the reflexive mig matches jag: känner mig trött.
titta always takes på for what you watch: tittar på TV.
en-words use min: min syster, min bil. Mitt is for ett-words.
Weather uses det as a placeholder subject: Det är kallt = it is cold.
"Barn" is an ett-word that stays the same in plural: ett barn, två barn.
på marks being at a place like a library: på biblioteket.
"Där borta" = over there. Place adverb first → verb second → subject third.
lägger mig literally lays myself down, the everyday way to say go to bed.
börja takes a plain infinitive, no att: börjar jobba = start to work.
ett-words use mitt: mitt hus. En-words use min instead.

english: We live on the third floor.
tip: Floors use på plus an ordinal: på tredje våningen = on the third floor.
